Q: sonar.coverage.exclusions and sonar.exclusions does not exclude the files from A:

Follow this procedure to exclude the files: Click on your project name in SonarQube -> Administration -> General Settings -> Analysis Scope -> Coverage Exclusions OR Source File Exclusions (You can put the file pattern in the text box)

This will skip the files which matches the given pattern.

Q: ValueError: No closing quotation A:

Make sure your ip is not "" or shlex will fail, cf Which exception to raise if a given string does not match some format?

Q: write and read from ttyUSB0, can't get response A:

If you are not cat'ing the USB0 device as you echo to it, then yes, you will not see its output because it has been and gone.

try something like:

tail -f /dev/ttyUSB0

and then echo stuff into it.

Q: What is object Buffer in Node.js? A:

<Buffer 50 4b 03 04 ...> is Node.js showing a Buffer object, which contains raw binary file data.

* Buffer = Node.js way to store binary data (bytes), not a string
* The hex values (50 4b 03 04) are just the file’s raw bytes
* 50 4b = “PK” → ZIP file signature

So yes, it’s the binary content of your zip file.

In React (browser)

You don’t get Buffer. You get a File or Blob:

const file = event.target.files[0];

To convert:

const arrayBuffer = await file.arrayBuffer();

If you really need a Node-style Buffer:

const buffer = Buffer.from(await file.arrayBuffer());

For S3 upload

You don’t need Buffer in frontend. Just upload the file directly:

s3.send(new PutObjectCommand({
  Bucket: "bucket",
  Key: file.name,
  Body: file
}));
